findings.checklist_item: [ ] Match idempotent signatures against stderr+stdout combined (mirroring delete_issue at acli.py:739), not stderr alone, so a 404/409 ACLI emits on stdout is still treated as idempotent.
evidence: acli.py:739 (the cited delete precedent) uses `err_text = (exc.stderr or "") + (exc.stdout or "")` then matches '404'/'not found' against the combined text
CalledProcessError is built as `CalledProcessError(p.returncode, full_cmd, out, err)` (acli_subprocess.py:486), so both exc.stdout and exc.stderr are populated
delete_issue_link runs without --json (acli_graph.py:637-648), so no structured stdout parse normalizes where the marker lands
findings.finding: The narrowed idempotent-signature match is specified against stderr only, but the sibling precedent the plan explicitly mirrors (delete_issue) matches idempotent markers across BOTH stderr and stdout because ACLI can emit diagnostics on stdout; a 404/409 written to stdout would be miscounted as a hard failure under the stderr-only rule.
findings.location: Approach step 1 ('stderr matching 404, 409, does not exist, or not found … absent stderr is NOT idempotent')
scenarios: A genuine concurrent-removal 404 that ACLI prints on stdout (not stderr) is classified as links_failed rather than idempotent applied — the exact benign-race case the plan says it wants to keep counting as applied
findings.suggested_fix: Change the idempotent test to inspect `(exc.stderr or '') + (exc.stdout or '')`; keep 'both streams absent is NOT idempotent' as the non-idempotent floor.
